# Effects and Power {#effects-power}

<div class="draft">Work in progress.</div>

## Two Worlds

- recap: Chapters \@ref(null-distributions) and \@ref(p-values) used only the null world (Steves exactly average); 5% of null t-values past cutoffs = alpha = Type I error rate
- now add a second world where Steves really are taller
- question flips: if the difference is real, how often does a group's t pass the same cutoffs? define: **power**

<div class="summary-box">
null world -> cutoffs -> how often do groups from the effect world pass those same cutoffs?
</div>

**What you need for this chapter**

- Chapter \@ref(t-statistic) (one-sample t-test), Chapter \@ref(null-distributions) (null distributions, cutoffs), Chapter \@ref(p-values) (p-values)

## A World With An Effect

- effect world: everyone mean 175 cm, SD 7; Steves mean 180 cm, same SD (made up but realistic)

```{r steve-effect-world, fig.cap="In the effect world, Steves' heights (dashed) sit 5 cm to the right of everyone's (filled). The heights are made up but realistic.", fig.alt="Two normal curves of height in centimetres. A filled curve for everyone is centred on a dotted line at 175. A dashed curve for people called Steve, the same shape, is centred on a solid orange line at 180.", echo=FALSE}
heights <- tibble(height = seq(150, 200, by = 0.5)) %>%
  mutate(
    everyone = dnorm(height, mean = 175, sd = 7),
    steves = dnorm(height, mean = 180, sd = 7)
  )

ggplot(heights, aes(x = height)) +
  geom_area(aes(y = everyone, fill = "Everyone"), alpha = 0.4) +
  geom_line(aes(y = steves, colour = "People called Steve"),
            linetype = "dashed", linewidth = 1) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 175, linetype = "dotted", linewidth = 0.9,
             colour = "grey20") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 180, linewidth = 0.9, colour = "#D55E00") +
  scale_fill_manual(NULL, values = c("Everyone" = "#467AAC")) +
  scale_colour_manual(NULL, values = c("People called Steve" = "#D55E00")) +
  guides(fill = guide_legend(order = 1), colour = guide_legend(order = 2)) +
  scale_y_continuous(NULL, breaks = NULL) +
  labs(x = "Height (cm)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r steve-effect-world-code, ref.label="steve-effect-world", eval=FALSE, webex.hide="Show the plot code"}
```

- still compare each group of 10 Steves with 175; null says Steves average, false in this world
- define: **Cohen's d** = difference between true mean and comparison value, in SDs

$$
d = \frac{\text{true mean} - \text{comparison value}}{\text{SD}}
$$

- Steves: (180 - 175) / 7 = `r round(5 / 7, 2)`
- rules of thumb: 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large; so medium-to-large, about 0.7 SD
- function for d comes later

## Build Both Distributions

- 1000 groups of 10 from each world
- null t-values and cutoffs from null world, as in Chapter \@ref(null-distributions)
- effect world: population mean 180, t still against 175
- second line becomes `my_effect_t()` later

```{r both-worlds}
null_ts <- replicate(1000, my_null_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 175, pop_sd = 7))
effect_ts <- replicate(
  1000, my_t_value(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), comparison_value = 175)
)

cutoffs <- my_cutoffs(null_ts)
cutoffs
```

```{r both-worlds-data, include=FALSE}
worlds <- tibble(
  t = c(null_ts, effect_ts),
  world = rep(c("Null", "True effect"), each = 1000)
) %>%
  mutate(past = ifelse(t < cutoffs[1] | t > cutoffs[2], "Past the cutoff", "Not past the cutoff"))
```

```{r both-histograms, fig.cap="1000 t-values from each world. The dashed lines are the cutoffs from the null distribution. Bars past the cutoffs are solid.", fig.alt="Two overlapping histograms of t-values. The null histogram is centred on zero; the true-effect histogram is centred a little above 2. About half of the true-effect histogram lies past the upper cutoff, and the rest overlaps the null histogram.", echo=FALSE}
ggplot(worlds, aes(x = t, fill = world, alpha = past)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.25, boundary = 0, position = "identity",
                 colour = "white") +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoffs, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Null" = "#467AAC", "True effect" = "#D55E00")) +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Not past the cutoff" = 0.3,
                                "Past the cutoff" = 0.9)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 8)) +
  labs(x = "t-value", y = "Count", fill = NULL, alpha = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r both-histograms-code, ref.label="both-histograms", eval=FALSE, webex.hide="Show the plot code"}
```

- notice: about half the orange t-values past upper cutoff; rest overlap the blue
- those groups came from the effect world but look like null-world groups

## Counting Dots

- same t-values as dots, one per group, so we can *count* them

```{r both-dots, fig.cap="The same 2000 t-values as dots. Solid dots are past the cutoffs.", fig.alt="Two horizontal strips of dots. The null strip is centred on zero with a few solid dots beyond the cutoffs. In the true-effect strip, about half the dots are solid, past the upper cutoff, and the rest are faded.", echo=FALSE}
ggplot(worlds, aes(x = t, y = world, colour = world, alpha = past)) +
  geom_jitter(height = 0.3, width = 0, size = 1.2) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = cutoffs, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Null" = "#467AAC", "True effect" = "#D55E00"),
                      guide = "none") +
  scale_alpha_manual(values = c("Not past the cutoff" = 0.25,
                                "Past the cutoff" = 0.9)) +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(-5, 8)) +
  labs(x = "t-value", y = NULL, alpha = NULL) +
  theme_minimal()
```

```{r both-dots-code, ref.label="both-dots", eval=FALSE, webex.hide="Show the plot code"}
```

- count solid and faded dots in each world:

```{r count-both}
null_past <- null_ts < cutoffs[1] | null_ts > cutoffs[2]
effect_past <- effect_ts < cutoffs[1] | effect_ts > cutoffs[2]

tibble(
  world = c("null", "effect"),
  past = c(sum(null_past), sum(effect_past)),
  not_past = c(sum(!null_past), sum(!effect_past))
)
```

- explain `|` = "or" (below lower *or* above upper); `!` = "not", so `sum(!null_past)` counts not past

```{r counts-table, echo=FALSE}
n_null_past <- sum(null_past)
n_effect_past <- sum(effect_past)
```

- four numbers fill a table of every outcome:

| | Not past the cutoff | Past the cutoff |
|---|---|---|
| **Null world** (Steves are average) | `r 1000 - n_null_past`: correct, no effect found | `r n_null_past`: **Type I error** (false positive) |
| **Effect world** (Steves are taller) | `r 1000 - n_effect_past`: **Type II error** (false negative) | `r n_effect_past`: correct, effect found |

- define: **alpha** = share of null groups past cutoff (Type I rate, chosen 5%)
- define: **beta** = share of effect groups *not* past cutoff (Type II rate)
- define: **power** = share of effect groups past cutoff; power is $1 - \beta$
- point out: only `r n_effect_past` of 1000 effect-world groups passed; found about `r round(100 * n_effect_past / 1000)`% of the time; real 5 cm difference missed about half the time
- alpha vs beta trade off via cutoffs: smaller alpha -> cutoffs out -> fewer null and fewer effect groups pass -> beta up, power down

- widget now has both worlds: blue = null (average Steves), orange = effect (taller)

<iframe class="demyst-widget" src="apps/nhst/embed.html?n=10&null=175&sd=7&mean=180&unit=cm" width="100%" height="960" title="Null and true-effect t distributions interactive widget" style="border: 0;"></iframe>

<script>

window.addEventListener("message", function (event) {

  document.querySelectorAll("iframe.demyst-widget").forEach(function (frame) {

  });

1. **Null +1000**, then **True +1** a few times: where do taller-Steve groups land?
2. **True +1000**: where do the histograms overlap? bars past cutoffs solid
3. **Show t-values as** -> **Dots**: table counts solid/faded per world, same four cells as above
4. change **True mean** (d updates; plot clears, rebuild both): share of orange dots past cutoffs?
5. change **Sample size**, rebuild: what happens to orange t-values with bigger groups?
6. **Alpha** -> .01, no rebuild: cutoffs move out; fewer null dots pass, fewer orange too

## Check It Against R

```{r my-effect-t-check}
set.seed(1)
mine <- my_effect_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 180, pop_sd = 7, comparison_value = 175)

set.seed(1)
r_version <- unname(
  t.test(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), mu = 175)$statistic
)

c(mine = mine, R = r_version)
all.equal(mine, r_version)
```

- point out: `pop_mean` = `comparison_value` gives `my_null_t()`; null world = effect world with effect zero

## Your Turn: Write `my_power()`

- power = proportion of t-values past cutoffs: one comparison, one mean

```{r my-power-exercise, eval=FALSE}
my_power <- function(ts, cutoffs) {
  past <-
  output <-
  return(output)
}

my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs)
```

`r hide("Show a hint")`
`past` is `ts < cutoffs[1] | ts > cutoffs[2]`, and `output` is `my_mean(past)`.
`r unhide()`

`r hide("Show one solution")`
```{r my-power-solution}
my_power <- function(ts, cutoffs) {
  past <- ts < cutoffs[1] | ts > cutoffs[2]
  output <- my_mean(past)
  return(output)
}

my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs)
```
`r unhide()`

- try on null t-values too:

```{r power-on-null}
my_power(null_ts, cutoffs)
```

- gives 0.05: "power" with no effect = Type I error rate

## Check It: Close Enough

- `power.t.test()` (base R) and `pwr.t.test()` (`pwr`) compute exact power from the t distribution
- `power.t.test()` takes raw difference (`delta` = 5 cm) and SD; `pwr.t.test()` takes Cohen's d

```{r power-check}
c(
  simulated = my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs),
  power.t.test = power.t.test(n = 10, delta = 5, sd = 7,
                              type = "one.sample")$power,
  pwr.t.test = pwr.t.test(n = 10, d = 5 / 7, type = "one.sample")$power
)

abs(
  my_power(effect_ts, cutoffs) -
    pwr.t.test(n = 10, d = 5 / 7, type = "one.sample")$power
) < 0.12
```

- within 0.12 of exact; bigger allowance than p-values in Chapter \@ref(p-values) because two things wobble (cutoffs from one simulation, effect t-values from another)

```{r exact-power, echo=FALSE}
exact_power <- pwr.t.test(n = 10, d = 5 / 7, type = "one.sample")$power
```

- n = 10, 5 cm difference (d = `r round(5 / 7, 2)`): exact power `r round(exact_power, 2)`
- found about `r round(100 * exact_power)`% of the time, missed about `r round(100 * (1 - exact_power))`%: roughly a coin toss, though Steves really are taller

## Your Turn: Write `my_cohens_d()`

- A World With An Effect used true mean and SD; with real data use sample mean and sample SD:

$$
d = \frac{\bar{x} - \mu_0}{s}
$$

- compare with t: bottom is SD, not SE
- t: distance relative to *noise in the mean*; d: relative to *spread of individual values*

```{r my-cohens-d-exercise, eval=FALSE}
my_cohens_d <- function(x, comparison_value) {
  mean_x <-
  sd_x <-
  output <-
  return(output)
}

my_cohens_d(scores, comparison_value = 46)
```

`r hide("Show a hint")`
`mean_x` uses `my_mean(x)`, `sd_x` uses `my_sd(x)`, and `output` is `(mean_x - comparison_value) / sd_x`.
`r unhide()`

`r hide("Show one solution")`
```{r my-cohens-d-solution}
my_cohens_d <- function(x, comparison_value) {
  mean_x <- my_mean(x)
  sd_x <- my_sd(x)
  output <- (mean_x - comparison_value) / sd_x
  return(output)
}

my_cohens_d(scores, comparison_value = 46)
```
`r unhide()`

## Check It: d And t

- no base R Cohen's d, but exact link to check: SE = SD / $\sqrt{n}$, so t = d times $\sqrt{n}$

$$
t = d \times \sqrt{n}
$$

- code the right-hand side for scores vs 46, compare with `my_t_value()`

```{r my-cohens-d-check-exercise, eval=FALSE}
d_times_root_n <-
c(d_times_root_n = d_times_root_n, t = my_t_value(scores, 46))
all.equal(d_times_root_n, my_t_value(scores, 46))
```

`r hide("Show a hint")`
Use `my_cohens_d(scores, 46)` for d, and `sqrt()` with `length(scores)` for $\sqrt{n}$.
`r unhide()`

`r hide("Show one solution")`
```{r my-cohens-d-check}
d_times_root_n <- my_cohens_d(scores, 46) * sqrt(length(scores))
c(d_times_root_n = d_times_root_n, t = my_t_value(scores, 46))
all.equal(d_times_root_n, my_t_value(scores, 46))
```
`r unhide()`

- same effect size, bigger sample -> bigger t -> more likely past cutoff
- why groups of 10 Steves often missed: d = `r round(5 / 7, 2)`, n = 10, effect t-values centre around `r round(5 / 7 * sqrt(10), 1)`, right next to the upper cutoff
- our scores: `r round(my_cohens_d(scores, 46), 2)` SDs above 46 (rules of thumb: 0.2 small, 0.5 medium, 0.8 large)

`r hide("Show what this section of my_functions.R should look like")`
```{r my-functions-after-2c-effects-power, eval=FALSE}
# Effects and Power --------------------------------------------------------
my_effect_t <- function(n, pop_mean, pop_sd, comparison_value) {
  sample_values <- rnorm(n = n, mean = pop_mean, sd = pop_sd)
  output <- my_t_value(sample_values, comparison_value)
  return(output)
}

my_power <- function(ts, cutoffs) {
  past <- ts < cutoffs[1] | ts > cutoffs[2]
  output <- my_mean(past)
  return(output)
}

my_cohens_d <- function(x, comparison_value) {
  mean_x <- my_mean(x)
  sd_x <- my_sd(x)
  output <- (mean_x - comparison_value) / sd_x
  return(output)
}
```
The rest of your file depends on which chapters you have done so far.
`r unhide()`

Then check that the saved file works on its own. This is the last chunk of the exercise file:

```{r toolbox-saved-check, eval=FALSE}
rm(list = ls())
source("my_functions.R")

set.seed(1)
mine <- my_effect_t(n = 10, pop_mean = 180, pop_sd = 7, comparison_value = 175)
set.seed(1)
r_version <- unname(
  t.test(rnorm(n = 10, mean = 180, sd = 7), mu = 175)$statistic
)
all.equal(mine, r_version)

all.equal(my_power(c(-3, -1, 0, 1, 2.5), c(-2, 2)), 0.4)

scores <- c(44, 47, 48, 49, 50, 50, 51, 52, 53, 56)
all.equal(
  my_cohens_d(scores, 46) * sqrt(length(scores)),
  my_t_value(scores, 46)
)
```

You should see three `TRUE`s:

```text
[1] TRUE
[1] TRUE
[1] TRUE
```
